title: WWT Partners Weekly Briefing
description: Cisco, Dell, HPE, NetApp, F5, Intel, NVIDIA, Microsoft, Palo Alto Networks, AWS, Google Cloud and VMware.
readFirst: Covers Oct. 26–Nov. 2. New: Tom's Hardware reported Oct. 31 that Intel is shifting some client wafer capacity to Xeon server processors. F5 had no new release. No new Dell, HPE, NetApp, or Microsoft release dated Oct. 30–Nov. 2 was found. No new VMware advisory dated Oct. 30–Nov. 2 was found; the Oct. 28 ESX logging bug remains due Nov. 11. Palo Alto's php2shell and Brotli hotfix notes from Oct. 29 remain the newest Palo Alto items. Cisco's Oct. 29 firewall KEV was dropped from the cyber page because its Nov. 1 due date has passed.

items.headline: Tom's Hardware: Intel is moving some client wafer capacity to Xeon server processors
items.summary: Tom's Hardware reported Oct. 31, citing Intel's earnings call, that Intel is moving some manufacturing capacity from client processors to data-center CPUs. Chief executive Lip-Bu Tan said the industry is navigating what he called one of the most significant supply shortages in history, driven by demand for super intelligence, and that Data Center and AI revenue was $7.3 billion in the third quarter of 2026, up 17 percent from the prior quarter. Chief financial officer Dave Zinsner said wafers being taken offline in Oregon to add Intel 3 capacity had been intended for Panther Lake client products on 18A. Tom's Hardware says that added Oregon capacity is expected to enter production in the second half of 2027, and that a Fab 24 expansion in Ireland for Xeon is not expected online until the end of 2027 unless it is accelerated.

items.headline: Cisco opens Model Foundry to partners and cites a WWT lab test of Deep Network
items.summary: Cisco said Oct. 26 at Partner Summit that Model Foundry, a service in Cisco Cloud Control, is in controlled availability for partners and can serve or fine-tune Cisco's domain models through an OpenAI-compatible API. Cisco said it tested the service with World Wide Technology and fine-tuned a 31-billion-parameter Deep Network model on troubleshooting data. WWT Chief Security Architect Naasief Edross said that fine-tune reached the right fix in 11 of 12 lab scenarios. Cisco's investor release the same day also said Cisco IQ for Partners is generally available, and the Model Foundry post names WWT in an early-access cohort for Cisco's open models.

items.headline: NVIDIA says RTX Spark laptops are on sale from Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft, and others
items.summary: NVIDIA said Oct. 28 that RTX Spark laptops are available from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft, and MSI. NVIDIA said the systems combine a Blackwell RTX GPU and a Grace CPU in one superchip with up to 128 GB of unified memory and up to 1 petaflop of FP4 AI performance, starting at $2,599, with 128 GB configurations on shelves. The same post said NVIDIA App can now split GPU resources between a foreground application and a background agent on RTX Spark. NVIDIA also said DGX Spark with 64 GB of unified memory, using the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip, is available from manufacturer partners.

items.headline: Palo Alto says php2shell is being exploited on internet-exposed management interfaces
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks updated its advisory on CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 on Oct. 29. Palo Alto now says active exploitation has been observed against management interfaces exposed to the internet, rates that case critical with a CVSS-B score of 9.2, and says the issue applies to PAN-OS on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and on Panorama. The Oct. 29 timeline entry says estimated dates for 11.1.7-h12 were removed because that version is released. The solution table says to upgrade PAN-OS 11.1.7 through 11.1.7-h* to 11.1.7-h12 or 11.1.16-h4 or later.

items.headline: Palo Alto's Oct. 29 Brotli update says the remaining listed hotfixes are released
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks updated its advisory on CVE-2026-111497 on Oct. 29. Palo Alto says the bug applies to PAN-OS on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls when Brotli inspection and TLS decryption are enabled on the dataplane, that the management interface is not affected, and that it is not aware of malicious exploitation of this issue. It says PAN-OS 11.1, PAN-OS 10.2, and Panorama are not affected, and that Brotli inspection is disabled by default in PAN-OS 11.2.4 and later. The Oct. 29 changelog says the estimated dates for 11.2.4-h23, 12.1.4-h13, and 12.1.10-h3 were removed because those versions are released, and the advisory says the same hotfix covers both the PHP bugs and Brotli except that 11.2.10-h16 fixes only PHP and 11.2.10-h17 fixes both.

items.headline: CISA adds a low-scored VMware ESX logging bug to the KEV catalog, due Nov. 11
items.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-41709, a VMware ESX insufficient-logging bug, to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Oct. 28, with a due date of Nov. 11. Broadcom's VMSA-2026-0006 rates the issue low, with a CVSS score of 2.7, and says a malicious administrator could perform certain operations without them being logged. The advisory lists fixed builds including ESXi-9.1.0.0-25370933, ESXi-9.0.2.0100-25595025, ESXi80U3j-25429389, and Cloud Foundation 5.2.4, and it lists no workaround. Broadcom credited Ian Barton of CrowdStrike.

items.headline: Broadcom: VMware SDDC Manager can be exploited through the Brotli bug, and patches are pending
items.summary: Broadcom's VMSA-2026-0008, issued Oct. 27, says Node.js in SDDC Manager has a remote-code-execution bug, CVE-2026-111497, because of an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder. Broadcom scores SDDC Manager 9.1.1 as critical, with a CVSS score of 9.8, and scores 9.0.x, 9.1.0, and 5.2.x as important, with a CVSS score of 7.5. The advisory says a malicious actor with network access to SDDC Manager may run arbitrary code, and that fixed versions are still pending. Workarounds are listed as KB460732 for 9.1.1 and KB460734 for the older releases. The affected lines are VMware Cloud Foundation and, on the 9.x rows, VMware vSphere Foundation.

items.headline: AWS Key Management Service adds the NIST ML-KEM post-quantum algorithm
items.summary: AWS said Oct. 26 that Key Management Service now supports ML-KEM, the Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism in NIST FIPS 203, which AWS says is meant to replace classical Diffie-Hellman and RSA key transport against a harvest-now, decrypt-later attack. Customers can use ML-KEM-512, ML-KEM-768 or ML-KEM-1024. AWS says the private key is held in FIPS 140-3 Level 3 hardware security modules and that the public key can be exported for local encapsulation with libraries such as AWS-LC, OpenSSL or Bouncy Castle. The feature is not available in the Middle East (UAE), Middle East (Bahrain) or China regions.
